title: Tea-Horse Station
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk, tea-caravan boss Cheng Yuan（A forty-year-old tea-caravan boss, dark-red headwrap, sheepskin jacket, copper scale-weight and horsewhip at the waist, booming voice, hands calloused by tea ropes） lifts the thick cotton door curtain into the tea warehouse hall（The tea warehouse hall of the tea-horse station, compressed tea bricks stacked along the walls, tack, tax plaques, and a branding furnace hanging from the beams） and sets the official tea brand（A copper official tea brand issued by the government, the two characters 'Border Tea' clear on the face, long handle wrapped in deep-brown leather strip） by a small stove to preheat.

Five butter lamps（A row of five butter copper lamps hanging under the tea-warehouse hall beams, flames steady, tea-smoke black marks on the bowl rims） hang under the tea-warehouse hall beams; Cheng Yuan trims each wick in turn, light falling on stacked tea bricks.

Two copper horse bells（Two copper horse bells hung inside the hall door beam, tongues polished bright, ringing clear when mountain wind passes the door） hang inside the door beam; Cheng Yuan taps them with a knuckle, and the ring carries through the hall.
Cheng Yuan presses the official tea brand onto damp cotton to test the heat; the characters 'Border Tea' rise clear in white steam.

Cheng Yuan unties a leather cord, opens the cowhide-covered tea-horse tax ledger（A cowhide-covered tea-horse tax ledger recording tea-brick counts, fodder accounts, porter silver, and mountain-pass clearance dates）, and checks tomorrow's tea-brick count for the mountain pass.
He looks up and counts the five butter lamps under the beams, confirming enough light before sealing the tea for the night.
Cheng Yuan sets the official tea brand beside the tea-horse tax ledger, ready to brand each pack after the mouths are sealed.

In the morning hitching yard（The hitching yard outside the station, wooden stakes in rows, hay and hoofprints on the ground, mountain trail visible at the far end）, Cheng Yuan greets young Xiaoman（A fifteen-year-old tea-worker girl, indigo waist sash, coral stud in the left ear, tea rope often wound on her wrist, bright clear eyes） leading tea packhorse Qiuli（A date-red tea packhorse named Qiuli, border-tea brand burned into the saddle flaps, symmetric tea-brick packs on both sides）, tea-brick packs hanging full on both sides of the saddle.
Xiaoman retightens Qiuli's girth, fingertips working through the saddle buckle and tea-rope knots.

Cheng Yuan lays out three tea-brick samples（Three corner-cut tea-brick samples bound with hemp rope, set on the tea-warehouse desk for checking grade and press marks） on the tea-warehouse desk, teaching Xiaoman to read press marks, cut corners, and stem thickness.
Xiaoman crouches beside Qiuli, studying the border-tea brand mark burned into the saddle flaps.

In the tea-inn alley（A narrow alley between the tea inn's wings, empty back-baskets and saddle pads stacked by the walls, courtyard light falling on blue stone slabs）, A-Du（A young caravan bookkeeper nearly identical in face to Xiaoman, but wearing silver-gray wrist guards and an ochre waist sash, cold hard eyes） in silver-gray wrist guards turns from behind empty back-baskets, face almost like Xiaoman's.
A-Du looks down through a hidden caravan bill; the ochre waist sash hangs by the blue stone slabs.
A-Du avoids the courtyard light and carries an empty tea pack through the end of the alley.
In the hitching yard, Xiaoman and A-Du brush past—one in an indigo waist sash, one showing silver-gray wrist guards.
Xiaoman tucks the coral stud into her hair; A-Du cinches the ochre waist sash tighter.
Both turn at once toward the horse train; nearly identical faces briefly overlap in the dusty light.
Months later on a mountain-rain night, Cheng Yuan keeps the fire alone in the tea warehouse hall; the official tea brand by the stove glows faintly red.

A bowl of strong tea is knocked over by the wind; the tea-horse tax ledger（The same tea-horse tax ledger soaked through with strong tea, cowhide cover sticky, vermilion numbers blurred into brown clumps） is soaked through, vermilion numbers blurred into brown clumps.
Cheng Yuan spreads the tea-horse tax ledger under a lamp to dry, then clears tea dust from the official tea brand's seams with a fine needle.
The spring tea season stretches long; every day Cheng Yuan weighs newly pressed tea bricks in the tea warehouse hall.
Before the Start of Summer, Cheng Yuan beats dust from saddle pads at the doorway; mountain-pass fog clings to the stone steps.
At autumn harvest, the caravan sorts damp tea packs in the hall; Cheng Yuan never takes his eyes off the branding furnace.
On a snowy night, Cheng Yuan wraps his sheepskin jacket tight and listens to distant horse-train bells drawing near.
Another New Year's Eve, only furnace fire and rows of tea bricks remain in the warehouse; Cheng Yuan locks the brand into an iron box.
At dawn, Cheng Yuan patrols the hitching yard; tea packhorse Qiuli grazes with head down, paired tea packs still hanging at the saddle.
Cheng Yuan bends to check Qiuli's shoes, girth, and saddle-flap brand mark.
He returns to the tea-warehouse desk and confirms those three tea-brick samples are still ranked by shade.

A gray mule（A blue-gray pack mule, saddle flaps without a border-tea brand, salt bags on its back instead of tea-brick packs） is led in by a porter, salt bags on its back, saddle flaps without a border-tea brand.
Afternoon storm pins the mountain pass; mud floods the hitching yard; the caravan hurries tea packs into the warehouse.

Cheng Yuan rushes over the threshold clutching the official tea brand（The same official tea brand, face cracked, the 'Border' character incomplete, deep-brown leather on the handle loose and curled）; the copper seal strikes a stone step and a crack bursts across the face.
Toward the pass, tea packhorse Qiuli charges with the last two tea-brick packs; the stone underfoot suddenly loosens.

Down the steep slope, tea packhorse Qiuli（Tea packhorse Qiuli has fallen dead on a steep slope, saddle flaps torn, tea-brick packs scattered, border-tea brand mark still clear） tumbles and falls dead; saddle flaps tear, tea-brick packs roll into the rain ditch.
Cheng Yuan stands in the rain gripping the cracked official tea brand, forbidding anyone to mix up the tack again.
The day after the mountain rain, Cheng Yuan writes on a blank page of the tea-horse tax ledger the hour tea packhorse Qiuli fell dead.
Qiuli's torn girth is hung on the tea-warehouse wall; Cheng Yuan stares a long time at that scrap of old leather.
Cheng Yuan packs Qiuli's saddle-flap shards into a wooden box, leaving only the brand mark face-up.
The five butter lamps under the beams remain; Cheng Yuan takes one to light Qiuli's old nameplate.
The cracked official tea brand lies on the desk; Cheng Yuan adds another line to the ledger for Qiuli's loss.
Weeks later, Cheng Yuan brings a tea-office coppersmith and sets a small furnace in the tea warehouse hall to recast the official tea brand.

The smith first holds up a forged brand（A forged brand shaped much like the official tea brand, but shallow inscription, no official plaque number, handle leather grayish） for comparison—shape close, but shallow inscription and no official plaque number.
Cheng Yuan watches the furnace mouth as copper fills the crack and the deep-brown leather is rewrapped tight.

After the new copper cools, the official tea brand（After recasting, the official tea brand's inscription is complete again, new copper a shade brighter, long handle rewrapped tight in deep-brown leather） inscription is complete; Cheng Yuan brands clear 'Border Tea' characters onto a scrap brick.

A porter carries a back-basket frame（A wooden back-basket frame bound with clay jars and straw rope, neither saddle flaps nor tea-brick packs） into the hitching yard, clay jars and straw rope bound on top—no saddle, no tea-brick packs.

A tea-tax clerk（A lean tea-tax clerk, also in a dark-red headwrap, but with an official plaque on his chest and bamboo tallies in hand, build close to Cheng Yuan's） walks in, also in a dark-red headwrap, but the official plaque on his chest swings plainly.
The tea-tax clerk points at the back-basket frame to check bamboo tallies; Cheng Yuan only tucks the recast official tea brand back to his waist.

From the kitchen comes a tea girl（A kitchen helper girl at the station, light-brown waist sash; at a glance like young Xiaoman, but green glass earrings and a shy gaze） in a light-brown waist sash; her profile at a glance looks like young Xiaoman, but she wears green glass earrings.
The tea girl practices coiling tea rope; Cheng Yuan reads her shy eyes and shakes his head, sending her to add firewood.

Years later at dusk, after a startled horse kicks him, Cheng Yuan（The same Cheng Yuan: left leg kicked by a horse, limping on a broken whip, sheepskin jacket mud-spotted, copper scale-weight still at the waist） limps on a broken whip to the abandoned tea-horse office（An abandoned tea-horse office yamen, empty main hall, flagpole snapped, grass on the stone steps, mountain wind through the broken door） door.
Two old horse bells still hang in the abandoned tea-horse office door beam; Cheng Yuan stops to hear them ring softly in the mountain wind.
Cheng Yuan lays a palm on the grassy stone steps, as if saying goodbye to the whole mountain trail.

By day, adult Xiaoman（A woman caravan boss in her early twenties, still in indigo waist sash and coral stud, tall and upright, palm marked by brand burns） returns along the mountain trail; the indigo waist sash clings to her short jacket in the wind.
Under the abandoned tea-horse office gate Xiaoman steadies limping Cheng Yuan and takes the copper scale-weight from his waist.
Beside the tea-office earthen kang, Xiaoman holds Cheng Yuan's gaunt hand and hears him explain the branding furnace's heat.

Cheng Yuan（Cheng Yuan has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the tea-office earthen kang, sheepskin jacket covering his chest, broken whip leaning by the bed）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and dies at the tea office.
Cheng Yuan's dark-red old headwrap still hangs behind the tea-office door; Xiaoman reaches out and gently brushes the dust away.

Adult Xiaoman nails the Cheng tea plaque（A wooden tea plaque nailed to a hall pillar, carved with 'Cheng Caravan Boss' and the year, edges blackened by tea smoke） back onto the tea-warehouse pillar; Cheng Yuan's year is still carved on it.
Xiaoman strokes Cheng Yuan's name on the Cheng tea plaque with a fingertip, then sets the recast official tea brand beneath it.

Disguised A-Du（Disguised A-Du still wears silver-gray wrist guards, a knife scar now at the brow, ochre sash replaced by an old leather belt） arrives from outside the tea-horse office, silver-gray wrist guards still showing at the cuffs, locking eyes with Xiaoman under the doorway.
Xiaoman and A-Du stand side by side in the empty hall—one steady in an indigo waist sash, one dull in an old leather belt.
The shot returns to years ago—the girl in an indigo waist sash learning tea-rope knots by a saddle appears again.
The opening moment returns—by the stove, that copper seal stamped 'Border Tea' first raises white steam.
Flash back to the early tea-inn alley—a figure in silver-gray wrist guards and ochre waist sash slips past empty back-baskets.
Before the eyes again: an old night when five oil lamps under the beams lit a wall of tea bricks.
Back to the yard of first meeting—wooden stakes in rows, the far end leading to the mountain pass; the smell of hay remains.
Xiaoman opens that tea-stained tea-horse tax ledger and stands in the tea warehouse hall resetting the caravan's departure day.
The five butter lamps under the beams still burn; Xiaoman looks up, finishes counting, then dims the flames.
Those three tea-brick samples on the desk are still ranked by shade; Xiaoman sets the recast official tea brand beside them.
